subject: Post-call: data access scoping, retention & break-glass next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Matt Chen <matt.chen@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: AuroraHealth Security <security@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 13:12:00 -0500
Subject: Post-call: data access scoping, retention & break-glass next steps

Thanks again for your time this morning, Matt — good conversation. I wanted to summarize the follow-ups we agreed on and call out a few clarifying questions so our security and solutions teams can prepare concise evidence and a draft runbook.

Recap (high level):
- Redwood would run inference for AuroraHealth in a dedicated VPC (Private deployment) with optional residency in us-east-1.
- You emphasized two constraints: (1) PII must be redacted at ingestion where possible and never retained past a defined retention window; (2) Support access must be strictly least-privilege with documented break-glass procedures.

Action items we agreed:
1) I’ll share a short data handling spreadsheet with columns for data type classification, retention window, and recommended controls (attached).
2) Your security team to confirm residency requirement (org-level vs. dataset-level) and whether encrypted backups are allowed in us-east-1.
3) We’ll draft a scoped support access runbook showing RBAC roles, JIT elevation flow, and audit logging examples.
4) Schedule a 30-min follow-up with your SecOps and our SRE to walk the runbook and simulation plan (proposed times below).

Clarifying questions (so we don’t over/under-spec):
- For retention: is the default policy 30 days for patient-identifiable fields, or do some datasets require shorter windows?
- For break-glass: do you require multi-person approval or is single-person emergency escalation acceptable for on-call?
- For logs: do you need full request/response logs stored for audits, or tokenized/hashed indices with sampled payload retention?

Proposed times for follow-up: Wed 11/04 10:00–10:30 ET or Thu 11/05 15:00–15:30 ET — I’ll defer to your security calendar.

I’ve attached the data-handling worksheet and our high-level SOC2 summary for context.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood-data-handling-sheet.xlsx, SOC2-Type2-summary.pdf
From: Matt Chen <matt.chen@aurorahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 17:45:12 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call: data access scoping, retention & break-glass next steps

Jonas — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers and new asks from our side.

Answers:
- Residency: we need PHI-hosted workloads to stay within the US, but our preference is region == us-east-1. Some non-PHI analytics datasets can live in us-west for cost balance; we’ll mark those in the spreadsheet.
- Retention: baseline is 14 days for patient-identifiable interaction logs; 90 days is acceptable for de-identified inference telemetry.
- Break-glass: emergency elevation must include two-step approval: (1) on-call engineer triggers break-glass, (2) Security Pager on-call must approve within 15 minutes. We need the approvals logged and immutable.
- Logs: we cannot store full PII payloads in plaintext logs. Storing tokenized identifiers or hashed keys with an audit index is acceptable; we may require secure, short-term escrow for full payloads during incident investigations (w/ KMS + strict ACLs).

New asks (please confirm):
- Provide an example RBAC matrix that maps Redwood roles to Aurora roles (support_read_only, support_jit_elevated, infra_ops).
- Draft runbook should include an example of simulated break-glass (steps + audit evidence produced).
- Can Redwood provide a sample audit log extract (anonymized) showing time, actor, action, and request-id? We’ll use it for our control mapping.

We can do Wed 11/04 10:00 ET for the SRE walk-through. I’ll add our SecOps lead (Deepa) to the invite if that works.

-Matt
Matt Chen
Head of Platform Security | AuroraHealth
matt.chen@aurorahealth.com

Thanks Jonas — quick status update and attachments (drafts).

What I’m attaching:
- support-access-runbook-draft.md (runbook with break-glass simulation steps and audit artifact examples)
- rbac_matrix_aurora.csv (RBAC mapping with actions & JIT flows)
- anonymized-log-sample.txt (log extract, tokenized IDs, request_id mapping)

Key points / assumptions in the artifacts:
- JIT Elevation: implemented via short-lived ephemeral credentials issued by Redwood Auth service; elevation request creates a unique approval ticket. Per Aurora ask, the Security Pager must call out approval ID; if not approved within 15 min, elevation is automatically revoked and the action is aborted.
- Break-glass flow: documented as two-phase (trigger -> Security Pager approval) and includes an immutable audit envelope containing the approval ticket hash, time, approver id, and the retained escrow pointer (if payload escrow was used).
- Logs: we show tokenization (SHA-256 truncated + salt) and include a retention TTL of 14 days for tokenized request payload indices; full payload escrow (encrypted, KMS-wrapped) is retained only for incident investigations and is only accessible via a documented request process that produces additional logs.

Open items before Wed 10:00 ET:
- Vivian: confirm the exact header fields Aurora wants in the audit extract (they asked for actor, action, request-id, approval metadata). If they want more, note it here.
- Jonas: confirm whether Aurora needs time-based residency enforcement at the dataset level (we currently can enforce region per model or per deployment).
- Monica: prepare the short slide (1 page) we can use in the walkthrough that shows: deployment topology, where logs are stored, and who holds KMS keys.

I’ll update the runbook after the walkthrough and produce a redline-ready doc to send to Aurora’s SecOps.

Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
